# Pūṣan, spelled the way the sources wrote it
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *pusan*. This is the file on how **Pūṣan** replaced it.

Pūṣan is the most companionable of Vedic gods: where others blaze, he accompanies. His myths are all journeys — of cattle, of brides, of the dead — and one memorable injury. Ṛgveda 10. 17 speaks to the dead with startling tenderness: "May Pūṣan take your hand and lead you; may the two Aśvins carry you in their chariot; go to the fathers, to the home that is yours.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Pūṣan
- **ASCII form:** pusan
- **Meaning:** "'The Nourisher' (from puṣ, to thrive), Vedic solar guide of roads"
- **Domain of influence:** Journeys, Nourishment, Roads
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** पूषन्
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 201 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Pūṣan** to *pusan* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **u → ū** — Macron marks the long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Pūṣan** lives at [/sites/pusan/](/sites/pusan/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/pusan/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/pusan/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/pusan/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Pūṣan** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Communication, Messaging & Logistics** — Lord of paths; the convoy and the escort, the road made safe.
- **Travel, Tourism & Place Branding** — The guide of roads; every journey’s escort since the Ṛgveda.
- **Pet Care & Animal Industries** — The herdsman; guardian of cattle on every road.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Sanskrit tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Rig Veda](/texts/rig-veda/) and [Ramayana](/texts/ramayana/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
